Read-only investigation in /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma VPS hosting platform). Do NOT edit any file. I am writing the deepest chapter of internal documentation about SERVER MIGRATION (lift-and-shift from a customer's old host onto an Nxeon VPS). I need VERIFIED facts with real `file:line` citations (absolute paths). Be extremely thorough — this is the flagship feature.

Read `/opt/nxeon/docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` first for context (do not edit it).

Investigate and report:

1. `worker/migrate-real.ts` (5351 lines) — enumerate the STEPS in order with the step names/labels the code actually emits and their line numbers. I need the full pipeline: pre-flight, storage estimate, package install, file copy, database dump/restore, docker image transfer, systemd unit migration, web server config generation, TLS/cert issuance, verification. For each step give the function name and line.
2. The VERIFICATION GATE in detail: how `sourceDomains` is derived, how the probe works (status + body), the default-page body signatures it rejects, the TLS SNI/CN/SAN check, what makes a domain "unserved", how `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` is computed, `outcomeReasons`, `blockers`. Exact line numbers.
3. The executable pre-flight before `systemctl enable` (ExecStart resolution) and the health gate (NRestarts sampling). Line numbers.
4. The heartbeat for long steps (~45s). Line numbers.
5. The web-server masking logic (apache2/httpd/caddy/lighttpd stopped+disabled+masked). Line numbers.
6. `worker/migrate.ts` (565 lines) — the wrapper. CONFIRM OR REFUTE the field-note claim that it "sets status: DONE unconditionally and persists only summary.results into Migration.items.results", and that the outcome reaches the customer only as the first entry of `results`. Quote the exact lines.
7. `worker/migrate-detect.ts` — the read-only auto-detection: what it detects, how it connects, what it writes.
8. `lib/actions-migrate.ts` — the server actions, the wizard steps, validation, the real-migration feature flag (is there one? where? what setting/env gates real vs simulated migration?).
9. The customer-facing screens: `app/dashboard/migrate/**` — describe the actual UI layout of each step (what fields, buttons, panels, progress display) precisely enough that I can draw an ASCII wireframe. Read the page/component files.
10. Admin surfaces for migration (search app/admin for migration).
11. Data model: the `Migration` model in prisma/schema.prisma — every field, and which fields are actually written vs never read.
12. Failure modes and how an admin would diagnose/re-run a failed migration (any re-run path in code? scripts/migrate-*.sh?).

Report every citation as /opt/nxeon/path:line. Flag anything simulated, stubbed, or written-but-never-read.

1	# Customer Migration — Field Notes & Failure Catalog
2	
3	Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
4	customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
5	migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
6	site serve over HTTPS with no server access.
7	
8	Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
9	HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS
10	(Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.18, 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 25 GB).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The architectural lesson
15	
16	**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
17	behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
18	source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP
19	bindings, and its certificate paths — none of which are valid on the target.
20	
21	Instead:
22	1. **Parse the source vhosts for intent** — server_name(s), document root or upstream
23	   proxy target, port, TLS on/off.
24	2. **Generate clean configs for the target's own web-server version.**
25	3. Leave the target's `nginx.conf` and include layout **intact**.
26	4. Copy the source config tree to a reference dir only
27	   (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/`), never into live config.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Failure catalog
32	
33	### Web server / routing
34	
35	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
36	|---|---------|---------|-----|
37	| 1 | Source `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's | `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared → a generated vhost is **silently ignored** | Write vhosts where the *live* `nginx.conf` actually includes; verify with `nginx -T \| grep <server_name>`, not just `nginx -t` |
38	| 2 | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` — nginx won't start | Rewrite source IP → target IP everywhere, or generate configs without IP binding |
39	| 3 | `/etc/letsencrypt` not migrated | 5 vhosts referenced missing certs + `options-ssl-nginx.conf` → config test fails → **web server down** | Migrate `/etc/letsencrypt` (certs, renewal conf, accounts) **or** strip TLS blocks and re-issue via certbot after DNS points over. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
40	| 4 | Web-server version mismatch | `http2 on;` (nginx ≥1.25) is an unknown directive on 1.18 | Detect target nginx version; translate/neutralise incompatible directives |
41	| 5 | Missing log directories | `open() "/var/log/apache2/domains/..." failed` | `mkdir -p` + `touch` every log path a config references before testing |
42	| 6 | Dead catch-all default server | Copied `listen <ip>:80 default; proxy_pass http://<ip>:8080;` hijacked everything → **502 on all traffic** | Detect copied default/catch-all servers whose upstream is dead; disable them |
43	| 7 | `listen` specificity beats `server_name` | An IP-bound block (`listen <ip>:80`) wins over generic `listen 80` regardless of server_name — our vhost never selected. **Repeated on 443** → wrong cert → `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` | Generated vhosts must bind the target's public IP explicitly on **both** 80 and 443 when copied configs do |
44	| 8 | Stale nginx PID after config swap | `invalid PID number "" in /var/run/nginx.pid`; `reload` fails | Use `restart` (not `reload`) after replacing nginx.conf; verify `systemctl is-active` |
45	| 9 | Multi-tenant wildcard subdomains | Tenant subdomains hit no server block → wrong cert | Add `server_name *.<domain>` when the app is multi-tenant (e.g. a `*_BASE_DOMAIN` env var). **A wildcard cert needs DNS-01** — HTTP-01 cannot issue `*.domain` |
46	
47	### Application startup
48	
49	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
50	|---|---------|---------|-----|
51	| 10 | Docker **images** not migrated | Standalone containers using locally-built images (`app/frontend:latest`, never in a registry) can never start | `docker save \| gzip` on source → stream → `docker load` on target. Prefer `docker pull` for public-registry images |
52	| 11 | App configured for the **old domain** | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`PUBLIC_API_URL` pointed at the old host — and frameworks like Astro/Next **bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time**. Page loads; nothing works | Detect old-hostname references in copied env; offer to rewrite **and rebuild** the affected image. A frontend calling the old server's API is a *silent* failure |
53	| 12 | Secrets in a non-standard env file | compose had `${VAR}` placeholders but no `.env` — real file was `prod.env` (used via `--env-file`) | Detect the env file the project actually uses; if placeholders would resolve empty, **refuse to start** and name the missing vars |
54	| 13 | Absolute binary paths differ between hosts | Migrated systemd units called `/usr/local/bin/node` (manual install on source); target has `/usr/bin/node` (apt) → unit crash-looped **880 times** | Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or rewrite the unit to the target's real path |
55	| 14 | Framework build artifacts don't transfer | Next.js `.next` copied but had no valid production build → `Could not find a production build` | Detect framework apps and run their build on the target (`next build`), or verify `BUILD_ID` exists before enabling the service |
56	| 15 | MySQL users & grants not migrated | Dump intentionally skips the `mysql` system schema, so **app DB users vanish** → access-denied despite data being present | Enumerate non-system users, `SHOW GRANTS`, replay `CREATE USER`/`GRANT` on the target preserving password hashes. (Postgres `pg_dumpall` already carries roles) |
57	| 16 | Stack-manager deployments | Apps deployed via Dokploy/Coolify/Portainer keep env/secrets in the manager's **own database**, not on disk (`/data/compose/<id>/`) | Detect the layout and warn explicitly — file copy alone will miss the secrets |
58	
59	### Storage / capacity
60	
61	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
62	|---|---------|---------|-----|
63	| 17 | `/var/lib/containerd` is a **separate store** from `/var/lib/docker` | Relocated `/var/lib/docker` to the attached volume; root **still** hit 100% — containerd had grown to 9.4 GB | Relocate/bind-mount **both**; add to `/etc/fstab`; verify with `df -h /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd` |
64	| 18 | Build cache is enormous | `docker builder prune -af` reclaimed **7.1 GB** after two builds | Prune after bring-up; retry once after pruning on ENOSPC before failing |
65	| 19 | Attached block volume unused | A 20 GB volume was attached but unformatted/unmounted while root filled | Detect an attached disk with no FSTYPE/mountpoint; format ext4, mount persistently by UUID, relocate the container stores onto it |
66	| 20 | Space estimate ignored Docker overhead | Guardrail estimated the ~11 GB file copy; image pulls/builds blew past it → `no space left on device` killed 2 of 3 compose projects | Include source image bytes + 1.5–2× build/ingest headroom; **re-check free space before the image phase**, not only at start |
67	| 21 | Small targets get starved | On 1 vCPU / 2 GB, a .NET + Astro build starved the box so hard the **QEMU guest agent stopped responding** | Don't assume the guest agent stays reachable during builds; keep the engine's SSH channel authoritative. Warn when target resources are small relative to detected workload |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Verification bar
72	
73	The final summary must distinguish **"migrated & running (verified)"** from
74	**"copied — needs a manual step"**, and verification must **HTTP-probe the real
75	hostname(s)** — not merely check that a port is listening. Never report success when
76	the site does not actually serve.
77	
78	Where full automation is genuinely impossible, say so **actionably** — name the file,
79	the value, and the command:
80	- wildcard TLS certs (need DNS-01),
81	- compiled-in API URLs (need a rebuild),
82	- stack-manager secrets held in the manager's database,
83	- standalone containers whose images aren't reproducible.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Same-OS question
88	
89	Matching the source OS removes a real class of problems (web-server/package version
90	and config-syntax incompatibilities — items 4 and some of 13), and the wizard
91	recommends it. **It is not a silver bullet**: items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14,
92	15, 17–21 are OS-independent migration-completeness issues.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 2026-07-25 — "reported SUCCESS, customer saw a certificate warning and an Apache default page"
97	
98	A real customer migration completed and reported success. The customer opened their
99	main site and got a browser certificate warning, clicked through it, and landed on
100	the **Apache2 Debian Default Page**. Six of their domains were dark. The run log
101	said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.
102	
103	Five separate failures, all now closed in `worker/migrate-real.ts`.
104	
105	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix (implemented) |
106	|---|---------|---------|-------------------|
107	| 22 | **The success metric could not fail** | Log line 1: `Sites actually serving: 4/4`. Log line 5: `Sites we could not publish automatically — content.revsports.ca, dealerleads.me, new.nexis.revsports.ca, reel.revsports.ca, stg.studionexis.com, studionexis.com`. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so it was 100% by construction | Denominator is now every hostname the **source** served, taken from its own live vhost config before we decide what we can publish (`sourceDomains`). The score is `served/total` against that set, the unserved ones are named, and a run with any unserved domain returns `outcome: "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` |
108	| 23 | **A 200 from the distribution's default page counted as "serving"** | The existing "make a real request to each domain" probe passed for a domain answering 200 with the Apache2 Debian Default Page | The probe now fetches the **body** as well as the status. Apache "It works!" / "Apache2 Debian Default Page" / "Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page" / "Apache HTTP Server Test Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies are all **not serving**. Content is only judged on a 2xx (a 301→HTTPS or a 404 legitimately has a tiny body); short JSON/XML bodies are exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |
109	| 24 | **TLS name mismatch was invisible** | `studionexis.com` was served `nexis.revsports.ca`'s certificate. Every visitor got a full-page security warning before reaching the site — and the probe used `-k`, so it saw only the status code | After each probe the certificate the server actually presents for that name is read with SNI (`openssl s_client -servername`), and its CN/SAN set is matched against the domain (`*.x` covers exactly one label). No coverage ⇒ **not serving**. Skipped when a container owns 443, where the proxy issues its own certificates after DNS moves |
110	| 25 | **`203/EXEC` — unit enabled with a binary that does not exist here** | `nexis-next.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node …`; the target has only `/usr/bin/node` (v20, apt). Crash-looped **78 times** and the migration still reported success | **Executable pre-flight before enabling anything.** Every `ExecStart` / `ExecStartPre` / `ExecStartPost` is parsed for its leading absolute executable (handling `-`/`@`/`+`/`!` prefixes, quoted paths, line continuations, `ExecStart=` list resets; PATH-resolved commands ignored). Missing ⇒ symlink to the same basename found via `command -v`, else copy the file from the source, else **do not enable it** and record a blocking entry naming the unit and the path |
111	| 26 | **"Never built" apps crash-loop silently** | `/opt/nexis` had no `.next` production build, so even with Node fixed the unit exits 1 forever | **Health gate after enabling.** Units settle, then `NRestarts` is sampled twice: `active` + a counter that is not climbing, or it is a blocker with the last journal lines attached. The Next.js `Could not find a production build in the '.next' directory` message is recognised by name and answered with `next build` |
112	| 27 | **Two web servers, one port 80** | `apache2` was re-enabled from the source's service list while we generated an nginx config. It could not bind 80 and sat `enabled + failed` — quiet until a reboot, where the race decides whether the site or the default page answers | When we generate our own configuration, every other host web server (`apache2`, `httpd`, `caddy`, `lighttpd` — or `nginx` when we chose Apache) is stopped, **disabled and masked**, and the run says so with the `systemctl unmask` command to reverse it. Step 11 also refuses to re-enable a web server from the source's service list when it is not the one we chose |
113	| 28 | **Ten minutes of silence at 89%** | The progress bar sat frozen while `apt-get install certbot` ran. A wedged migration and a slow one looked identical | The three genuinely long steps — package install, image transfer, certificate issuance — run inside a heartbeat that emits one line every ~45s naming what is still running and for how long |
114	
115	### The point about #25
116	
117	**This failure was already in this document.** It is item 13, written up after an
118	earlier migration where the same `/usr/local/bin/node` mismatch crash-looped a unit
119	880 times, with the fix spelled out: *"Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or
120	rewrite the unit to the target's real path."*
121	
122	It recurred anyway, on a different customer, four months later — because a documented
123	fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file. **That is why #25 is now an
124	executable pre-flight check that runs before every `systemctl enable`, not a
125	paragraph.** The general rule this establishes: a failure mode that has been observed
126	twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
127	approximately nothing.
128	
129	### Outcome semantics
130	
131	`runRealMigration` now returns `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus
132	`outcomeReasons`, `sourceDomains`, `unservedDomains` and `blockers`. A migration is
133	`COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` when any domain the source served does not serve here, when
134	any domain could not be checked, or when any migrated unit is not running.
135	
136	`Migration.status` in `prisma/schema.prisma` is a plain `String` (not a Prisma enum),
137	but the only writer is `worker/migrate.ts`, which sets `status: "DONE"`
138	unconditionally and persists **only** `summary.results` into `Migration.items.results`.
139	So the outcome is also emitted as the **first entry of `results`** — step
140	`Migration outcome: COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, status `failed` — which is what actually
141	reaches the customer's screen today. Wiring `summary.outcome` through to
142	`Migration.status` / a dedicated column is a one-line change in `worker/migrate.ts`
143	that has not been made.
144
